::::: {#chapter-1 .chapter}
## Chapter 1: Do light and fire synergistically control stand density?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](photos/chapter1.jpg){fig-alt="Researcher is kneeling and measuring the height of a bolting longleaf pine tree"}
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
This chapter of my dissertation is on-going, involving a multi-year observational study set up in the Sandhills of North Carolina. This work aims to determine:

- How does light availability relate to growth of bolting longleaf pines?
- How does size relate to survival?

:::
::::
:::::

::::: {#chapter-2 .chapter}
## Chapter 2: How does pyrophytic oak density relate to fuel load and fuel bed composition, and therefore flammability?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
![](photos/chapter2.jpg){fig-alt="Longleaf pine savanna at golden hour, with the understory of grasses and forbs glowing golden in the setting sun"}
:::
::: {.column width="5%"}
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
I have just started working on this chapter of my dissertation. This work aims to determine:

- How does pyrophytic oak density relate to the fuel load and the relative abundance of fuel types in the understory?
- How does the fuel load and relative abundance of fuel types shape fuel bed flammability and fire behavior?
:::
::::
:::::
